name: Memento (Agent-on-the-Fly / AgentFly) - Fine-tuning LLM Agents without Fine-tuning LLMs
venue: arXiv preprint (arXiv:2508.16153, cs.LG/cs.CL); submitted 22 Aug 2025, v2 25 Aug 2025; not peer-reviewed at time of writing
authors_affiliation: Huichi Zhou, Yihang Chen, Siyuan Guo, Xue Yan, Kin Hei Lee, Zihan Wang, Ka Yiu Lee, Guchun Zhang, Kun Shao, Linyi Yang, Jun Wang. Primary affiliations: AI Centre, University College London (UCL) and Huawei Noah's Ark Lab (UK); also Jilin University and Institute of Automation, CAS. Corresponding authors: Linyi Yang (SUSTech) and Jun Wang (UCL).
code_url: https://github.com/Agent-on-the-Fly/Memento (MIT license; ~2.4k stars; both non-parametric CBR and parametric memory/neural retriever code released)
task_domain: Deep-research LLM agents: long-horizon tool-use, planning, and decision-making over open-domain QA and web research (spans QA / web / tool-use / planning).
problem_setting: Adaptive generalist LLM agents that must continually adapt from environmental feedback without fine-tuning (no gradient updates to) the underlying LLMs. Interactive, online/test-time setting: an agent solves complex long-horizon tasks by iteratively planning, invoking external tools, and processing heterogeneous data. Single-agent (planner-executor) architecture; supervision is sparse binary task-level reward (success/failure) rather than dense step labels. Both successful and failed trajectories are stored. Continual/online learning: the case bank is built from scratch and grows during deployment.
what_is_retrieved: Past experiences stored as cases: case triplets (state s = task, action a = plan, reward r = success/failure label). At planning time the planner retrieves the K nearest/highest-value past cases (problem-solution-outcome episodes) from the Case Bank.
retrieval_grounding: GROWING / episodic memory the agent writes (an online-growing Case Bank built from the agent's own trajectories), explicitly contrasted with classic RAG over a STATIC document corpus. Note: tool-level execution also uses live web search/crawl over external sources, but the case retrieval that defines the method targets the agent's own episodic memory.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Fixed top-K case selection (K nearest cases by similarity, or top-K by learned Q-value). The objective is a precision/utility-driven small selection: ablations show performance peaks at K=4 and plateaus or declines for larger K (small, high-quality memory preferred over many exemplars), so it is closer to a precision-driven selection than a recall/completeness objective.
cbr_cycle_coverage: [Retrieve, Reuse, Revise, Retain] - all four canonical CBR phases are implemented. Eq. 2 explicitly labels the trajectory factorization as (1) Retrieve, (2) Reuse & Revise, (3) Evaluation, (4) Retain, (5) Transition. Reuse/Revise = LLM adapts the retrieved plan; Retain = append new case to Case Bank.
explicit_cbr_grounding: True. The work explicitly frames itself as case-based reasoning (CBR), citing Aamodt & Plaza (1994), Kolodner-lineage CBR, and prior CBR agents (DS-Agent, Guo et al. 2024/2025). It states it is 'the first to cast case-based continual learning for LLM agents' and contrasts CBR with modern RAG.
retrieval_unit: case (problem-solution tuple): a triplet (s, a, r) where s = task/state, a = plan, r = binary success reward. Effectively a (state, action/plan, reward) experience tuple stored as episodic memory; only the final-step (s_T, a_T, r_T) of each trajectory is written to keep the bank compact.
index_source: Growing episodic memory induced online/at test-time (Case Bank Mt built from scratch and incrementally appended during deployment); not an offline static corpus. For OOD experiments the bank is pre-populated from training-split trajectories, then queried at inference.
index_structure_topology: Flat vector index: states are encoded with a frozen text encoder (SimCSE) and stored as vectors keyed by their (a, r) payload; retrieval is nearest-neighbour over this flat embedding store (cosine similarity for non-parametric; Q-value scoring over the same flat bank for parametric).
retriever_type: Non-parametric variant: dense embedding nearest-neighbour (SimCSE encoder + cosine similarity, off-the-shelf). Parametric variant: learned retriever - a neural case-selection policy (Q-function as a two-layer MLP over SimCSE state representations) realising a learned soft-Q retrieval policy. So: dense (off-the-shelf) and/or learned value-based retriever.
retriever_learning_signal: Non-parametric: none (off-the-shelf similarity). Parametric: RL / value-based - a neural case-selection policy trained via online soft Q-learning in a maximum-entropy RL framework. The optimal retrieval policy is a softmax over the optimal Q-value; Q is learned by TD learning (kernel/episodic-control estimate) or, in the single-step deep-research instantiation, by supervised binary cross-entropy regression of Q(s,c;theta) onto the binary task reward r in {0,1} (downstream-task-effectiveness signal).
query_construction: The query/key is the current task instruction encoded as the state s_t (raw task text passed through the frozen SimCSE encoder). No sub-query decomposition for case retrieval; the raw task state is the query. (Task decomposition into subtasks happens downstream in the planner after case retrieval.)
query_granularity: Task-level: case retrieval is performed at the planning step keyed on the task/state. Because CBR is applied only for planning, the deep-research instantiation collapses to a single-step (per-task) setting; retrieval is essentially one-shot at the task/plan level (re-issued on replanning).
when_to_retrieve: One-shot per planning step (retrieve relevant cases when the planner forms/refines a plan). The planner can replan if a task is unfinished, so retrieval can recur across plan-replan iterations, but it is not token-level or uncertainty-triggered active retrieval.
retrieval_trigger_signal: Fixed schedule tied to the planning stage: the planner queries Case Memory at the start of planning (and again on replanning when the task is judged incomplete). No learned router, token-confidence, or reflection-token trigger for case retrieval.
reranking: For case retrieval: no separate cross-encoder reranking stage; the parametric Q-function effectively reranks candidate cases by learned Q-value (TopK over Q). For tool-level web search, retrieved candidate web results are re-ranked by semantic similarity to the query context (a tool-internal reranking, distinct from case retrieval).
retrieved_context_refinement: Case side: minimal - retrieved case triplets are concatenated verbatim with the current task instruction to form the planner prompt (no decompose/compress of cases). Tool side: a query-aware crawler (ai_crawler) performs content compression to reduce token cost, and search results are filtered/re-ranked; these refine tool outputs rather than retrieved cases.
tool_document_engineering: Tools are exposed via the Model Context Protocol (MCP) as a suite of MCP servers (search, crawl, code, document/image/video/audio/excel/math). Tool selection is performed by the LLM executor at execution time from MCP tool descriptions; no special synthetic-query augmentation or instruction-tuned tool embeddings are reported for tool indexing.
index_content_separation: Partial: memory stores compact case triplets (only final-step s,a,r; state vectorised, action/reward kept as text) so a lightweight retrievable representation is kept; heavy per-subtask tool logs are kept in separate Tool Memory and subtask results in Subtask Memory (text-based), separating high-level case index from per-step execution content.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: Tools integrated via a live, model-agnostic MCP (Model Context Protocol) layer; executor acts as an MCP client invoking MCP servers (SearxNG metasearch, SerpAPI, Crawl4AI, code sandbox, etc.). Tool index is the configured MCP server list (extensible by adding FastMCP servers); not a CRUD-auto-synced live registry.
tool_dependency_awareness: N/A - retrieval does not explicitly model inter-tool dependency graphs; the LLM executor composes tools per subtask using Tool Memory, but there is no dependency-graph/bipartite-KG modeling of tool prerequisites.
how_retrieved_used: Prompt augmentation + case adaptation: retrieved case triplets (s_i, a_i, r_i) are concatenated with the current task instruction and fed to the planner LLM, which reuses and revises (adapts) the retrieved plans to generate a new plan (in-context, no weight updates). Mixes successful and failed cases so the agent can prospectively reuse successes and retrospectively avoid past mistakes.
planning_integration: Retrieve-then-plan within a plan-and-act loop: the CBR planner retrieves cases, generates a plan / decomposes the task into subtasks; a tool-enabled executor (MCP client) runs each subtask; the planner then assesses completion and replans with updated context. CBR is applied at the planning stage (one-shot exemplar-style case conditioning at plan time), looped with execution.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Case retrieval is per-plan (per-task / per-replan) rather than per-token. Tool calls are per-subtask within the executor's autonomous episode (per-tool-call within a rollout). So two granularities: case retrieval at plan level; tool invocation at subtask/step level.
adaptation_mechanism: LLM-prompted adaptation of retrieved cases (Reuse & Revise): the planner LLM conditions on retrieved (s,a,r) cases to produce an adapted plan; execution-feedback-driven revision via replanning when subtasks are incomplete. Case selection itself is additionally RL-shaped by the learned Q-function in the parametric variant, but the case content adaptation is LLM in-context (no LLM fine-tuning).
retrieved_item_representation: Structured case triplet injected as text: (state/task, plan/action, success-or-failure reward). The state is also stored as a SimCSE embedding for retrieval; the surface form injected into the planner is the natural-language task + plan + outcome (raw trajectory final-step), i.e. a structured note rather than a distilled rule or executable skill.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Raw (final-step) trajectory case = a single past problem-solution-outcome episode, including both successes and failures. Not a distilled strategy/guideline, not an executable skill/program, not a reusable abstract workflow - it is a concrete past case used analogically.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Two mechanisms: (1) the learned value-based (parametric) case-selection policy prioritises high-utility cases, mitigating noise from irrelevant cases (soft-Q / maximum-entropy retrieval); (2) deliberately small K (peak at K=4) to limit injected noise (ablation shows large K hurts). Storing failure cases also provides corrective signal. No retriever-aware SFT of the base LLM or explicit relevance evaluator/self-reflection module for cases.
memory_type: episodic (an episodic Case Bank of past trajectory cases). Has both non-parametric (vector NN store) and parametric (Q-function-shaped) variants; auxiliary Subtask Memory and Tool Memory are text-based working memories.
write_back: True. The system stores new experiences as cases: Write appends (s_t, a_t, r_t) to the Case Bank; in the parametric variant Write also online-updates the Q-function (and an episodic memory D of (s,c,Q) tuples). Case bank grows incrementally into a transferable experience repository.
online_growth: True. The Case Bank is an online-growing store that expands during deployment/test-time (built from scratch over iterations); it is not frozen after an offline induction phase. Continual-learning curves show monotonic improvement across iterations as cases accumulate.
write_back_trigger: On both success and failure - both successful and failed trajectories are written to the case bank (enabling prospective reuse of successes and retrospective avoidance of mistakes). In the planner-executor implementation a case is written upon task completion (final-step s_T,a_T,r_T of each trajectory), with the binary outcome as reward; parametric variant additionally updates the Q-function on each write.
failure_experience_usage: Success + failure: the memory accumulates both successful and failed cases; retrieval returns a mixture of successful and failed cases, and the binary reward (r in {0,1}) lets the value/policy down-weight failure cases while the LLM can use failures to avoid past mistakes. Not success-only.
memory_evolution_update: Append-only for case content (cases are added each step; only final-step tuples stored to keep the bank compact, deduplicating redundant intermediate states). The retrieval policy evolves: in the parametric variant the Q-function/kernel is continually refined (delta-update via TD/CE learning and target-network soft updates), reshaping the retrieval distribution over the growing bank. No explicit forgetting/pruning of stored cases is implemented (noted as future work / memory-compression TODO).
retrieval_as_learned_policy: Yes (in the parametric variant). Retrieval/case-selection IS a learned policy: a neural case-selection policy over the episodic case bank, formalised in a Memory-augmented MDP (M-MDP) and optimised via online soft Q-learning (maximum-entropy RL; optimal policy = softmax over learned Q). The non-parametric variant uses fixed similarity top-K. This is the paper's defining contribution and matches the field's M-MDP soft-Q-learning exemplar.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: Single-agent private episodic memory (one growing Case Bank for the agent). The bank is transferable across tasks/datasets (e.g. OOD transfer from training to test datasets) but the paper does not implement shared memory across multiple distinct agents or heterogeneous frameworks.
benchmarks: GAIA (validation 150 / test 300, 3 difficulty levels); DeepResearcher suite of 7 open-domain QA datasets - Natural Questions (NQ), TriviaQA (TQ), HotpotQA, 2WikiMultiHopQA (2Wiki), MuSiQue, Bamboogle, PopQA; SimpleQA (4,330 fact-seeking Qs); Humanity's Last Exam (HLE, 2,500 Qs).
benchmark_family: tool/long-horizon agentic (GAIA); multi-hop & open-domain QA / web research (DeepResearcher = NQ/TQ/HotpotQA/2Wiki/MuSiQue/Bamboogle/PopQA); factual QA (SimpleQA); frontier/long-tail academic reasoning QA (HLE). Overall: web/tool-use + multi-hop QA families.
baselines: GAIA leaderboard agents: Alita, Skywork Super Agents, Langfun Agent, AWorld/Aworld, Manus, OWL-Workforce/OWL-Roleplaying, OpenAI DeepResearch, Open Deep Research, Su Zero Ultra, h2oGPTe Agent. DeepResearcher table: CoT, CoT+RAG, Search-o1, Search-r1 (base/instruct), R1-Searcher, DeepResearcher (training-based SOTA). SimpleQA: WebSailor, WebDancer, WebThinker, DeepSeek-r1-React. HLE: GPT-5, Gemini-2.5-Pro, o3-high, o4-mini-high. Internal ablation baselines: Offline Executor, Online Executor, Memento w/o CBR.
key_metrics: GAIA: accuracy / Exact Match (and Pass@3 on validation), reported per level and average. DeepResearcher/SimpleQA/HLE: macro-F1 and PM (Partial Match, GPT-4o-mini-judged semantic match). Plus token cost / cost-per-task analysis on GAIA.
headline_result: Top-1 on GAIA validation with 87.88% (Pass@3) and 79.40% on the GAIA test set (open-source agent frameworks, as of June 26 2025). On the DeepResearcher 7-dataset suite: 66.6% F1 / 80.4% PM (weighted avg), surpassing the training-based SOTA DeepResearcher (51.8 F1 / 60.5 PM); case-based memory adds +4.7 to +9.6 absolute points on OOD tasks; 95.0% on SimpleQA; 24.4% PM on HLE.
ablations: (1) Component-wise (Table 5): Offline Executor -> Online Executor (live tools) -> +planning (Memento w/o CBR) -> +CBR; CBR gives consistent additive gains (HLE +4.5 F1/+7.0 PM, SimpleQA +3.7/+5.3, DeepResearcher +6.7/+8.2). Planning alone gives large gains; live tools help on SimpleQA/HLE but hurt DeepResearcher F1 (-18.0, attributed to contamination). (2) K sweep (Table 3): peak at K=4 (64.5 F1/78.5 PM), plateau/decline for larger K -> small high-quality memory beats more exemplars. (3) Continual-learning over 5 iterations (Table 4): Parametric CBR (80.46->85.44) > Non-Parametric CBR (79.84->84.85) > w/o CBR (78.65->84.47). (4) OOD generalisation: +4.7-9.6 absolute on MuSiQue/Bamboogle/PopQA when bank trained on NQ/TQ/HotpotQA/2Wiki. (5) Token-cost analysis on GAIA by difficulty level.
evaluation_decoupling: No - intrinsic retrieval metrics (Recall@k / nDCG / case-retrieval accuracy) are not reported separately; evaluation is end-to-end task performance (accuracy/F1/PM). The K-sweep and parametric-vs-non-parametric ablations indirectly probe retrieval quality but via downstream task metrics, not intrinsic retrieval metrics.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Primarily outcome metrics (final-answer EM/F1/PM/success). Process is examined only indirectly: continual-learning curves over iterations, token-cost-per-task by GAIA level, and per-task-type statistics (code/search/crawl). No formal step-wise reasoning-faithfulness or retrieval-precision scoring.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Core claim is low-cost continual adaptation with no LLM fine-tuning / no gradient updates to the base LLM (only a small two-layer MLP Q-function is trained in the parametric variant). Token-cost analysis on GAIA: per-task input/output tokens scale with difficulty - Level 1 ~26k/4.7k, Level 2 ~48k/6.9k, Level 3 ~121k/9.8k; main cost is integrating multi-step tool outputs. A query-aware compression crawler is added to reduce token cost. Small K=4 keeps retrieval cost low.
context_budget_and_selection_count: Fixed-K case selection, K=4 used as default (best on DeepResearcher); ablated K in {0,1,2,4,8,16,32} with peak at K=4. Repo default MEMORY_TOP_K=8 with max 8 positive / 8 negative examples for parametric memory. Reranked-then-truncated via TopK over Q-values (parametric) or TopK over cosine similarity (non-parametric). No explicit token-budget cap on injected cases reported.
survey_scope_and_axes: N/A - this is a method/system paper, not a survey.
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A - this is a method paper, not a benchmark paper. (It uses existing benchmarks: GAIA 450 Qs across 3 levels; DeepResearcher 7 datasets at 512 examples each except Bamboogle 125; SimpleQA 4,330; HLE 2,500.)
builds_on: Case-Based Reasoning (Aamodt & Plaza 1994); episodic / neural episodic control (Pritzel et al. 2017); maximum-entropy / soft Q-learning RL (Haarnoja et al. 2017, 2018); plan-and-act paradigm (Erdogan et al. 2025); prior CBR agents DS-Agent and Guo et al. (2024/2025); deep-research agent setting (Huang et al. 2025); Model Context Protocol (MCP) for tooling; SimCSE sentence encoder; tool stack (SearxNG, Crawl4AI, Camel-AI toolkit).
contrasts_with: Contrasts with (a) parametric continual-learning agents that fine-tune the LLM via SFT/RL (e.g. Search-r1, R1-Searcher, DeepResearcher, START) - high compute, catastrophic forgetting; (b) static handcrafted-workflow / reflection agents (Reflexion, ReAct-style) lacking lifelong learning; (c) classic RAG over static document corpora (Lewis et al. 2020) which lacks continual adaptation; (d) memory agents that append cases without curation (swamping problem) and other memory systems (MemoryBank, SAGE, Mem0, A-MEM, MemInsight, ExpeL, AutoGuide, Agent Workflow Memory, Agent-KB, Alita).
lineage: Group D: case-based planning / experience-and-memory-augmented agents. Sits in the lineage of CBR-for-LLM-agents and memory-augmented continual-learning agents, distinguished by formalising planning as a Memory-augmented MDP (M-MDP) with retrieval/case-selection AS a learned soft-Q policy over a growing episodic case bank (vs fixed similarity top-k), bridging episodic/neural-episodic-control RL with deep-research LLM agents.
